question: Which Linux companion app architecture and ownership path should OpenClaw pursue now that Windows Hub has shipped?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug: multiple unmerged Linux implementations exist, and the choice affects native dependencies, security review, packaging, release ownership, and long-term app maintenance.

options.title: Choose one Linux track first
options.body: Select a canonical Linux architecture and require the chosen PR to satisfy gateway-contract, packaging, proof, and security gates before merge.

options.title: Keep multiple prototypes open
options.body: Let C/GTK, Rust/GTK, and desktop/Tauri experiments continue, accepting slower review and duplicated security analysis.

options.title: Defer Linux companion work
options.body: Close or pause implementation PRs until the project has capacity for native Linux app ownership and security review.

recommendation.title: Choose one Linux track first
recommendation.body: Select a canonical Linux architecture and require the chosen PR to satisfy gateway-contract, packaging, proof, and security gates before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He provided the strongest product-direction signal in the issue discussion and has recent native-app history across existing companion surfaces.
